subject.title: fix(session-memory): forward hook config model to LLM slug generator

question: Should OpenClaw accept `hooks.internal.entries.session-memory.model` as a supported hook-level config contract for LLM slug generation?
rationale: The patch is technically narrow, but it turns an open-ended passthrough value into user-visible provider/model routing behavior that can affect existing configs after upgrade.

options.title: Accept hook model contract
options.body: Treat `session-memory.model` as the supported slug-generation override and merge after normal exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Require upgrade docs first
options.body: Ask for explicit public docs or release-note wording before merge so the newly consumed key and routing effect are clear.

options.title: Pause this direction
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers want slug routing solved somewhere other than hook-level config.

recommendation.title: Accept hook model contract
recommendation.body: Treat `session-memory.model` as the supported slug-generation override and merge after normal exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and commit metadata make him the clearest history-backed owner for the session-memory and slug-generator behavior under review.
